builds.name: Reference: Ranked mid core
builds.goal: Reference for Ahri: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ mid players use most (8,138 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 53.2% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A mobile pick mage who uses Charm to create brief damage windows, then repositions to chase takedowns or escape. The current mid provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Malignance → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass. Electrocute keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Sorcerer's Shoes, Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff.
builds.summary: The proven mid baseline: Malignance → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass, with Electrocute.
testPlan: Play it in mid as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Malignance → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 53.2% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Malignance → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

kitEvidence.formula:
Killing minions or monsters grants Ahri an Essence Fragment. After obtaining [9] Fragments, Ahri consumes them to restore [characterLevelInterpolation(35 → 95; raw flags preserved) + (0.2) × AP] Health.

When Ahri scores a takedown against an enemy champion within [3] seconds of damaging them, she feasts upon their Essence, restoring [characterLevelInterpolation(75 → 165; raw flags preserved) + (0.3) × AP] Health.

Ahri releases 3 fox-fires that seek nearby enemies and deal [40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage, reduced to [(40 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 120 + (0.4) × AP) × (0.4)] damage beyond the first. She also gains [40]% Move Speed decaying over [2] seconds.

Ahri nimbly dashes, firing [3] essence bolts at nearby enemies, prioritizing champions. These bolts deal [75 / 125 / 175 + (0.35) × AP] magic damage each. Spirit Rush can be Recast up to 2 more times within [15] seconds.

Consuming a champion's Essence with Essence Theft during this period extends the recast window by up to [10] seconds and grants an additional recast of Spirit Rush (up to [3] stored).
Ahri throws then pulls back her orb, dealing [35 / 60 / 85 / 110 / 135 + (0.5) × AP] magic damage on the way out and [35 / 60 / 85 / 110 / 135 + (0.5) × AP] true damage on the way back.
Ahri blows a kiss that Charms the first enemy hit for [1.2 / 1.35 / 1.5 / 1.65 / 1.8] seconds and deals [80 / 120 / 160 / 200 / 240 + (0.85) × AP] magic damage.

builds.name: Dash-weave chase
builds.summary: Turn Spirit Rush into spaced attack windows.
builds.goal: Turn Spirit Rush into spaced attack windows.
builds.hypothesis: Fox-Fire grants 40% decaying speed and Spirit Rush permits three initial dashes over 15 seconds. Nashor's Tooth rewards actual attacks; Dusk and Dawn adds one Spellblade attack and repeats on-hits. AP still powers Charm and both Orb passes, so the attack experiment retains spell damage.
testPlan: Required state: Need Charm connected, an isolated target and time between dashes for attacks.
Compare attacks landed and total damage over one moving-target R chase at equal gold.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Lost burst can prevent the first takedown and its healing/recast reward.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Three dash casts do not guarantee three independently ready Spellblade procs.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Nashor's Tooth, Dusk and Dawn, Cosmic Drive, Rabadon's Deathcap, Cryptbloom, Sorcerer's Shoes. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Survive the engage
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Ahri: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A mobile pick mage who uses Charm to create brief damage windows, then repositions to chase takedowns or escape. Does a Charm-led spell sequence or additional real attacks between dashes win the pick? Separate R access/reset value from a stationary combo. A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
builds.summary: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
testPlan: Kit question for Ahri: Does a Charm-led spell sequence or additional real attacks between dashes win the pick? Separate R access/reset value from a stationary combo.

Start with the early core (Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Ahri sends out and pulls back her orb, dealing magic damage on the way out and true damage on the way back. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.
The route fails Ahri's stated kit question: Does a Charm-led spell sequence or additional real attacks between dashes win the pick? Separate R access/reset value from a stationary combo.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.
Full cost 16,000 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Banshee's Veil, Rylai's Crystal Scepter, Void Staff are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.

builds.name: Return-orb finisher
builds.summary: Exploit the return pass against armored targets.
builds.goal: Exploit the return pass against armored targets.
builds.hypothesis: Orb of Deception has 0.5 AP on each pass, with true damage returning. Shadowflame explicitly enhances magic and true damage below 40% health; Cosmic Drive triggers on either type, letting W speed and R relocation steer the return. Void Staff supports the other magic hits rather than penetrating true damage.
testPlan: Required state: Keep the target intersecting both Orb paths and push below Shadowflame's threshold before return.
Measure outbound and return separately above and below 40%, then repeat versus different MR.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Dashes away from the return path or shields can erase the proposed finish.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Magic penetration does not increase Q's true damage half.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
